detailed_findings.finding: The truncation argument for computing [q^j] is valid because the product has finitely many factors and every factor has only nonnegative exponents.
The expansion by subsets S and multiplicity choices m_i correctly yields monomials with sign (-1)^{|S|} and exponent sum_i m_i i + sum_{s in S}(r+s).
The bijection between multiplicity families (m_i) and finite multisets lambda of elements of I is correct, and the finiteness of X_j is adequately justified.

reason: The proof matches the stated combinatorial coefficient-extraction lemma. It correctly truncates each geometric series when extracting [q^j] because all exponents are nonnegative, expands the resulting finite product by subsets S and choices of multiplicities m_i, and then identifies those multiplicity families with finite multisets lambda of elements of I. The resulting signed enumeration is exactly the definition of X_j, and finiteness of the indexing set is justified. No forbidden or undeclared dependencies are used.
